name: Monument
one_liner: Online alcohol treatment by video: a doctor can prescribe medication, plus therapy, mostly paid by insurance at about $25 a visit.
best_for: Adults who want to cut back or stop drinking with a doctor's help, without going to a clinic
People with in-network insurance (e.g. Cigna/Evernorth, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare/Optum) in a state Monument serves
People who want medication for alcohol plus optional therapy by video
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People at risk of severe alcohol withdrawal (seizures, DTs) who need medically supervised detox
People outside the states Monument serves
People who want treatment for opioids or other drugs
People who want a phone app (care is through a web portal)
short_description: Video visits with doctors and therapists for cutting back or stopping drinking; about $25 a visit with insurance or $100 self-pay, in some states.
long_description: Monument (which took over Tempest's members) is a US telehealth practice that began as an online alcohol treatment program and now also advertises therapy and doctor visits for depression and everyday illnesses. For alcohol, you start with a video visit with a physician, who asks about your drinking and medical history and decides whether medication-assisted treatment is safe; therapy based on cognitive behavioral therapy and motivational interviewing can be added in 'Total Care' plans. Monument says most people pay $25 per video appointment with in-network insurance (it lists UnitedHealthcare/Optum, Cigna/Evernorth, Aetna and Medicare in some states) and $100 per session self-pay. An October 2026 review counted seven states. In 2024 the FTC and DOJ charged Monument with sending users' health information to Meta and Google for advertising from 2020 to 2022 without consent; a court order now bans it from sharing health data for advertising. No published study of Monument's own program was found.
patient_summary: You sign up online, choose your state and insurance, and meet a doctor by video who checks whether medication for drinking is safe for you; therapy sessions can be added. With in-network insurance most visits cost about $25; without it a session is $100. It is only offered in some states, and it now also offers general therapy and doctor visits.

pricing.notes: Monument's homepage says most people pay $25 per video appointment with insurance; its FAQ gives a flat $100 per session self-pay rate. In-network carriers vary by state (UnitedHealthcare/Optum, Cigna/Evernorth, Aetna, Medicare listed). Older $14.99 community and $199–$299 monthly plans are no longer advertised.

basis.regulatory_action: FTC/DOJ order, 2024: shared users' health data with Meta and Google for advertising without consent (2020–2022); now banned from sharing health data for ads

privacy.notes: FTC/DOJ 2024 order after Monument sent health data to ad platforms; its notice says it no longer discloses health information for advertising and that it is not a HIPAA covered entity but voluntarily follows HIPAA. Website policy on ad cookies and deletion not confirmed.

faqs.q: What's included in Monument's treatment program?
faqs.a: Monument includes physician-prescribed medication (if appropriate), unlimited therapist-led group sessions, personal coaching sessions, and community support. You choose your level of engagement based on your needs and goals.

No, Monument supports various goals—complete abstinence, moderation, or simply 'drinking less.' You define success based on what's right for you. Their approach is harm reduction focused rather than abstinence-only.

Monument's Essential plan (groups and community) starts around $14.99/month. Full plans with medication and coaching are $199-299/month. Some insurance plans are accepted. Financial assistance may be available.

Monument physicians prescribe FDA-approved medications for alcohol treatment, primarily naltrexone. Medication reduces cravings and the rewarding effects of alcohol, making it easier to cut back or stop.

primary_uses: Medication to reduce drinking, prescribed by video
Therapy for cutting back or quitting alcohol (CBT, motivational interviewing)
Using insurance for online alcohol treatment
General therapy and doctor visits in some states

availability.note: Only in some US states (a review checked in October 2026 counted seven); pick your state at sign-up. Took over Tempest's members.
